newsitem.title: NORWAY: Norway debt weakens amid overseas EMU worries.
newsitem.headline: Norway debt weakens amid overseas EMU worries.

text.p: Norwegian debt weakened with German Bunds on Monday because of talk overseas that Europe's single currency project might be delayed.
But the spread to Bunds narrowed two points.
"It is Germany that is dragging Norway in a negative direction," one dealer said. "There were no Norwegian factors in today's development. The action went as expected."
He said the market digested a two billion crown expansion of Norway's government 2001 bond with ease. The highest accepted yield was 4.66 percent.

Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said in an analysis that the Norwegian economy was expected to grow above the European average again in 1997, supported by relatively buoyant private consumption and high investment.
"This will continue to put pressure on the inflation rate, although the expiry of temporary factors will lower the annual rate during the course of the year," it said.
Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said the economy was expected to grow by around three percent in both 1997 and 1998. It said its inflation forecast remained above two percent in 1997.
The analysis said the crown would continue to be supported by strong economic growth although a further weakening of the oil price would take off some of the pressure.

"The 10Y bond yield spread over Bunds has traded in a range around 0-20 basis points over the last month. A further decrease in the oil price could be negative for the bond market. However, the supply situation is very favourable," Deutsche Morgan Grenfell said.
